article_title: The Effect of Enriched Creative Activities Program Supported with Aytürk Technique on Creativity Level in Music Courses
citation: Ayşen Ertürkler and Hakan Bağcı. (2019). The effect of enriched creative activities program supported with Aytürk technique on creativity level in music courses. Educational Research and Reviews. https://doi.org/10.5897/ERR2019.3692
title: Enriched Creative Activities Program structure: rhythmic-table activities culminating in student-produced musical products
description: The program is a 10-week sequence of activities in which each session uses the Rhythmic Table and ends with a creative product. Students mind-map concepts, combine selected words or symbols into rhymes, place them in a 16-cell table, and turn the table "into rhythmic or melodic structures in symbols or words." Products were presented to other students in classrooms, at the schoolyard or the conference hall, and videotaped. The first six activities used the book Oynayalım Eğlenelim; later activities included Creating Our Own Brand, professions of the next century, and Living with Robots.
requirements: A Rhythmic Table of 16 cells distributed to students
Familiarity with the table from initial activities
Group work and teacher class management
constraints: Allocated time may not be long enough
It wanders away from the educational process in the presence of contests, competitive feelings, or winners and losers
target_learning_goals: creative thinking
rhythm and musical expression
self-expression
examples: Activities were performed in an experimental class of 18 students in 40 minutes for 10 weeks; some families volunteered to play fun rhythm games with their children at home

article_title: Improving Resilience and Self-Esteem among University Students with Entrepreneurship Simulation Board Game
citation: Prihadi, K., Cheow, D. Z. Y., Yong, J. H. E., & Sundrasagran, M. (2018). Improving Resilience and Self-Esteem among University Students with Entrepreneurship Simulation Board Game. "RE and SE are the predictors of opportunity pursuing styles (also called action characteristics in Frese's model) to be more Schumpeterian or Kirznerian." The model further suggests RE and SE are affected by individuals' experience, with their relationship mediated by practical intelligence. It builds on Frese's Action-Characteristics Model of Entrepreneurship.

constraints: Developed from a qualitative study of TBG among teenagers; quantitative validation of SE contribution was lacking prior to this study

resilience
self-esteem
examples: Used as the theoretical framework motivating the current study's hypotheses about TBG frequency effects

article_title: Efficacy of Enrichment Triad and Self-Direct Models on Academic Achievement of Gifted Students in Selected Secondary Schools in Nigeria
citation: Fakolade, O. A. & Adeniyi, S. A. (2010). Efficacy of Enrichment Triad and Self-Direct Models on Academic Achievement of Gifted Students in Selected Secondary Schools in Nigeria. International Journal of Special Education, Vol 25 No 1. https://www.internationaljournalofspecialeducation.com
title: Renzulli's Enrichment Triad Model: three interrelated enrichment types moving students from awareness to process skills to product development
description: The Enrichment Triad Model, developed by Renzulli, is a framework for qualitatively different gifted programmes that moves "the student through awareness, the learning of process, and the development of a product using three different but interrelated types of learning activities." Type one uses interest centers, field trips, and guest speakers to create awareness; type two builds process skills such as brainstorming, categorization, and synthesis; type three involves students investigating real problems, with the teacher managing the process. The study used it as one of two treatment instructional models.
requirements: Teachers guide students to identify problems consistent with the students' interests and acquire the methodological resources and investigative skills needed to solve them
constraints: Renzulli notes qualitatively different programmes mean more than freedom of choice, lack of pressure, absence of grading, or individualization of pace, although all are important
target_learners: gifted and talented secondary school students
target_learning_goals: academic achievement in English language and Mathematics
investigative attitude and problem-solving skills
examples: In the study, gifted students went through 13 weeks of English language and Mathematics sessions taught through the Enrichment Triad model as part of the treatment package

description: An achievement test prepared by the researchers to measure academic success in teaching English vocabulary. It was developed after interviews with 11 experts from English language teaching, teaching, assessment and evaluation, and curriculum and instruction, initially consisted of 25 questions, and after validity and reliability analysis "the test had 17 questions". It was administered to all 43 participants as pre-test and post-test.
requirements: Expert review and validity and reliability analysis were part of the test development procedure
constraints: Prepared by the researchers for this study's topics and age group

examples: The test was conducted to the participants (n= 43) as pre-test and post-test after being reduced from 25 to 17 questions

article_title: On Reading Comprehension Teaching for English Majors under Relevance Theory
citation: Ping He. (2018). On Reading Comprehension Teaching for English Majors under Relevance Theory. English Language Teaching, 11(1). https://doi.org/10.5539/elt.v11n1p46
title: Enrich learners' target-culture knowledge to reduce the cognitive effort of reading inference
description: Because language carries culture, the article recommends building students' knowledge of English-speaking cultures (biblical culture, history, custom, politics, education) so that more mutual knowledge with the writer accelerates inference of the writer's intentional information. It argues that "With more mutual-knowledge about English culture, readers will pay less cognitive efforts", while acknowledging Sperber and Wilson's criticism that the mutual-knowledge hypothesis is untenable in its strong form.
requirements: A certain amount of mutually known cultural context between reader and writer
constraints: Chinese students cannot fully share mutual knowledge with English native speakers; mutual knowledge cannot be activated exactly as the communicator intends
target_learners: Chinese college English majors learning English as a foreign language
target_learning_goals: English reading comprehension
inference of writer's intended information
examples: The article's curriculum context: Chinese students are indoctrinated with English grammar and lexical knowledge throughout their learning period, leaving cultural knowledge limited
key_sources: Ping He. (2018). On Reading Comprehension Teaching for English Majors under Relevance Theory. English Language Teaching, 11(1). https://doi.org/10.5539/elt.v11n1p46

article_title: The Effect of a Social-Emotional School-Based Intervention upon Social and Personal Skills in Children and Adolescents
citation: Tania Gaspar, Ana Cerqueira, Cátia Branquinho & Margarida G. Matos. (2018). The Effect of a Social-Emotional School-Based Intervention upon Social and Personal Skills in Children and Adolescents. Journal of Education and Learning, 7(6). https://doi.org/10.5539/jel.v7n6p57
title: School-based SEL approaches are more effective when they include the entire school, use interactive methodologies and become part of the school culture
description: The article states that school-based approaches to promoting social and emotional wellbeing gain effectiveness from whole-school design: "School-based approaches seem to be more effective when they include the entire school", using a social skills promotion model, peer education, student participation and initiative, interactive and participated methodologies, and integration into the school culture. New programs should be integrated into existing ones, with community partnerships encouraged.
requirements: Use of a social skills promotion model, peer education, and student participation and initiative
Interactive and participated methodologies integrated into school culture
constraints: The article presents this as a synthesis of prior effectiveness research (Jané-Llopis & Barry, 2005), not as a finding tested in this study
target_learners: All pupils in a school, including risk groups such as low-SES, migrant and low-education adolescents
target_learning_goals: Social-emotional competence, pro-social behavior, health and wellbeing
examples: The article cites studies suggesting problem solving is the best short-term strategy for promoting pro-social behaviors, while peer mediation provides long-term success

article_title: Parent Beliefs and Student Absences: Large Absence-Reduction Field Experiment
citation: Todd Rogers, Avi Feller. (2016). Parent Beliefs and Student Absences: Large Absence-Reduction Field Experiment. SREE Spring 2016 Conference Abstract. https://www.sree.org/conferences/2016/
title: Encourage + Self + Norms attendance mailing intervention and four-condition experimental design
description: A mailed-communication intervention tested in a major metropolitan district (about 200 schools, about 30,000 students). Households were randomly assigned to one of four conditions: a no-outreach Control, an Encourage mail stressing attendance importance and parental efficacy, an Encourage + Self mail adding the student's number of missed days, and an Encourage + Self + Norms mail adding comparison to "the typical student in their school and grade". The design tests the added impact of each component, since Norms cannot be evaluated without implicitly measuring Encourage and Self.
requirements: Random assignment of households; only one targeted student per household to avoid cross-treatment contamination; opt-out consent procedure
constraints: When a Norms-assigned student had fewer absences than classmates, the Encourage + Self mailing was sent instead, so condition effects reflect being sent at least one mailing of that type
target_learners: Guardians of students in grades 1-12 who were absent more than 2 days above the modal student
target_learning_goals: Reduced student absences through improved guardian information and engagement
examples: Table 1 reports total sample sizes of 7,664 (Control), 7,679 (Encourage), 7,670 (Encourage + Self), and 7,666 (Encourage + Self + Norms), totaling 30,679 students

article_title: Experiential Learning: Improving the Efficacy of an Undergraduate Business Degree
citation: Frank DeSimone and John Buzza. (2013). Experiential Learning: Improving The Efficacy Of An Undergraduate Business Degree. American Journal Of Business Education, 6(1). http://www.cluteinstitute.com/
title: Entrepreneurial venture start-up experiential component
description: In Monmouth University's Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management courses, "the students all participate in the start -up of an entrepreneurial venture, encompassing all phases of the operation including legal, finance, marketing, and management." Students work in teams with assigned tasks and timelines to launch a company within the semester using real money from a university grant, with the option to buy back the company for $1.00 afterward. Professor Buzza acts as CEO, guiding and aiding students throughout, and students give a formal end-of-semester presentation on the company and their process. In fall 2011 the class created and presented a GPS Tracking company.
requirements: All students participate (no control group); teams with assigned tasks and timelines; professor acting as CEO providing guidance and support; university grant funding
constraints: Because all students participate, the article states there was no control group to assess potential improvement of the typical Monmouth student
target_learners: undergraduate business students, majority management majors
target_learning_goals: critical thinking
entrepreneurship
business decision making across functional areas
examples: The fall 2011 cohort of 67 students launched a GPS Tracking company and presented it formally at semester's end
key_sources: Frank DeSimone and John Buzza. (2013). Experiential Learning: Improving The Efficacy Of An Undergraduate Business Degree. American Journal Of Business Education, 6(1). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1054187

article_title: A Comparative Study of English Language Teaching Practices at the Access Program and Public Schools
citation: Iqbal, M., & Rafi, M. S. (2018). A Comparative Study of English Language Teaching Practices at the Access Program and Public Schools. Bulletin of Education and Research, 40(3), 231-249. https://pu.edu.pk/journals/index.php/ber/
title: The English Access Microscholarship Program
description: The Access Program is a U.S. State Department-funded after-school English program for socio-economically disadvantaged youth aged 13–20, implemented in more than 80 countries and in Pakistan since 2004. It is "an after school progra m for two years, that requires minimum of 360 instructional hours", with classes of five or ten hours per week plus intensive sessions in a "threat -free environment". Students learn the four language skills, gain exposure to U.S. culture, train in computers and critical thinking, and take part in community service. The study evaluated its ELT practices against public school teaching.
requirements: Providers verify students' socio-economic status, organize classes by proficiency level and a two-year age range, keep the program gender-balanced, and schedule classes so they do not interfere with regular school
constraints: Classes must be between one and three hours per day, and the program requires a minimum of 360 instructional hours over two years
target_learners: Socio-economically disadvantaged youth aged 13–20 in Pakistan
target_learning_goals: English language skills (reading, writing, speaking, listening), computer literacy, critical thinking, and exposure to U.S. culture and democratic values
examples: In Pakistan the program is implemented through non-profit providers in cities including Lahore, Faisalabad, Multan and Sargodha, with over 16,000 graduates reported by 2015

title: End-to-end case study simulation pattern spanning the radiotherapy patient pathway within a single module
description: A module-level instructional pattern in which a single IMRT-related treatment site (head) is carried through the full radiotherapy pathway — pre-treatment CT imaging and immobilization, data transfer, treatment planning in the TPS, and delivery on a linear accelerator — replacing a prior procedural workbook method that used multiple body-site cases. The single-scenario design was chosen "to maintain simplicity and consistency" and to avoid the additional costs of custom-designed phantoms for different body sites.
requirements: Equipment at key stages: CT scanner/simulator, Eclipse TPS, and VERT platform, with the phantom integrated at each stage
constraints: Less favoured alternative of multiple phantoms for different body sites due to additional costs and a preference for a single scenario
target_learning_goals: Practical skills and theoretical understanding across the full radiotherapy planning pathway
examples: The hosting HEI's revalidated PRPS module delivers the head-site case end-to-end across scheduled simulation sessions
key_sources: Genitsarios Ioannis, Jhagra Robin, Warn Clive, Xavier Jesrina Ann. (2025). From classroom to clinic: innovating radiotherapy treatment planning education through real-world end-to-end case study simulation with an anthropomorphic phantom. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-06695-w

article_title: The impact of the educational environment on student engagement and academic performance in health professions education.
citation: Kassab Salah Eldin, Rathan Ramya, Taylor David C. M., Hamdy Hossam. (2024). The impact of the educational environment on student engagement and academic performance in health professions education. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-06270-9
title: Design learning environments to foster cognitive and behavioral engagement and support students' academic self-perceptions
description: Because cognitive and behavioral engagement were the engagement dimensions that predicted academic achievement, the article recommends educators "prioritize the development of a supportive learning environment that actively fosters these forms of engagement". It specifically advises integrating curricula that enhance students' academic self-perceptions, such as confidence in academic success and active learning strategies, and fostering a positive atmosphere with openness, psychological safety, and belonging to strengthen emotional engagement.
requirements: Curricula and teaching that build students' confidence in academic success and use of active learning strategies; social support networks, constructive feedback, and meaningful peer relationships
constraints: The supporting evidence is cross-sectional and associational; the study measured average engagement across courses and relied solely on student self-reports
target_learners: health professions education students in undergraduate programs
target_learning_goals: student engagement in learning and academic achievement (GPA)
examples: The article recommends culturally responsive teaching strategies and taking cultural differences into account when designing educational interventions, based on the nationality differences in DREEM scores
key_sources: Kassab Salah Eldin, Rathan Ramya, Taylor David C. M., Hamdy Hossam. (2024). The impact of the educational environment on student engagement and academic performance in health professions education. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-06270-9

article_title: Academic Performance, Health and Support Needs: Comparing Foster Care Alumni and Peers in Higher Education in Norway.
citation: Lehmann Stine, Hysing Mari, Sivertsen Børge. (2024). Academic Performance, Health and Support Needs: Comparing Foster Care Alumni and Peers in Higher Education in Norway. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph21111470
title: Provide enduring financial and social support policies for care-experienced students through young adulthood and specifically in higher education
description: The article argues that because foster care alumni students face higher economic burden, poorer health and higher unmet support needs, "policies need to be put in place to ensure that care-experienced students receive adequate support through their young adulthood and specifically in higher education". It points to the need for enduring financial support to ameliorate disadvantages from lacking parental figures, and for early prevention efforts targeting mental and somatic health alongside financial and social support.
requirements: Support must extend through young adulthood, not end at age 18, since after-care receipt drops substantially by age 21
constraints: Extended care policies show mixed results internationally, and extended foster care appears to predict enrollment but shows no effect on degree completion in cited studies
target_learners: young adults transitioning out of foster care
target_learning_goals: higher education attainment and completion
retention and prevention of drop-out
examples: The SHoT2022 national survey found foster care alumni students reported less parental financial help (21.3% vs 41.9%) and more financial problems (43% vs 24.3%) than peers, while 25.0% reported unmet needs for special academic assistance
key_sources: Lehmann Stine, Hysing Mari, Sivertsen Børge. (2024). Academic Performance, Health and Support Needs: Comparing Foster Care Alumni and Peers in Higher Education in Norway. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph21111470

article_title: The effect of spaced E-Learning on knowledge of basic life support and satisfaction of nursing students: a quasi-experimental study.
citation: Ranjbar Fataneh, Sharif-Nia Hamid, Shiri Maryam, Rahmatpour Pardis. (2024). The effect of spaced E-Learning on knowledge of basic life support and satisfaction of nursing students: a quasi-experimental study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-05533-9
title: Encoding Variability Theory as the mechanism account for the spacing effect
description: The article presents Encoding Variability Theory as the theoretical basis for spaced learning and the spacing effect. It states that "The 'Encoding Variability Theory' posits that varying learning conditions activate distinct areas of the brain, facilitating improved information retrieval from memory", and that repeating stimuli at longer intervals fosters assimilation, retention and recall. The study's spaced E-learning intervention is framed as an application of this theory to BLS training for nursing students.
requirements: Learning content must be repeated at intervals rather than presented all at once for the theorized variability in learning conditions to operate
target_learning_goals: long-term retention of procedural knowledge such as basic life support
examples: The intervention group received BLS training across three one-hour sessions on consecutive days, operationalizing spaced learning informed by the theory.

article_title: Trainee anaesthetist self-assessment using an entrustment scale in workplace-based assessment.
citation: Castanelli Damian J, Woods Jennifer B, Chander Anusha R, Weller Jennifer M. (2024). Trainee anaesthetist self-assessment using an entrustment scale in workplace-based assessment. Anaesthesia and Intensive Care. https://doi.org/10.1177/0310057X241234676
title: Entrustment scales as a scaffold for shared understanding of performance standards between trainees and supervisors
description: The article frames self-assessment as a social learning strategy in which peers and supervisors help learners make sense of performance data, rather than personal unguided reflection. The entrustment scale aligns assessment ratings with everyday supervisory decisions about how much independence to grant, so that the question of how much supervision is required conveys the desired performance standard. The authors conclude that the scale "does provide a scaffold for a shared understanding of performance standards between trainees and supervisors", supported by the substantial concordance they observed.
requirements: Ratings must be made independently by trainee and supervisor before discussion for the concordance to be meaningful
constraints: The study focused on anaesthesia and the authors state they cannot know how applicable the results are to other specialties with different work and assessment practices
target_learners: postgraduate anaesthesia trainees in workplace-based assessment
target_learning_goals: accurate self-assessment of performance
judging the level of supervision required for safe clinical practice
self-regulated learning towards independent practice
examples: ANZCA introduced trainee self-assessment into workplace-based assessments using a nine-point entrustment scale with parallel supervisor and trainee descriptors
key_sources: Castanelli Damian J, Woods Jennifer B, Chander Anusha R, Weller Jennifer M. (2024). Trainee anaesthetist self-assessment using an entrustment scale in workplace-based assessment. Anaesthesia and Intensive Care. https://doi.org/10.1177/0310057X241234676

article_title: EndoTrainer: a novel hybrid training platform for endoscopic surgery.
citation: Hernansanz A, Rovira R, Basomba J, Comas R, Casals A. (2023). EndoTrainer: a novel hybrid training platform for endoscopic surgery. International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11548-023-02837-x
title: EndoTrainer: hybrid physical-virtual endoscopic training platform with sensor-based measurement, automatic evaluation and AR interactivity
description: EndoTrainer is a hybrid surgical training platform combining a physical anatomy module with real surgical tools, an endoscopic camera and a Tool Tracker Arm that measures endoscope position, together with real-time evaluation, personalised curricula and augmented-reality feedback. The article describes it as "a physical platform containing the specific anatomy, real surgical tools, endoscopic camera and the required sensors to measure users actions" plus the capability "to evaluate users performance". It was validated with hysteroscopic exercises from the GESEA Certification Programme.
requirements: Modular anatomical reproduction must be exchangeable to reproduce different scenarios and specialties
Sensors and actuators in the exercise module cavities to measure user interaction
constraints: Validation to date is limited to basic hysteroscopic exercises; Exercise 2 (Hand-eye Coordination) is out of the scope of the paper
Code and data are proprietary to SurgiTrainer
target_learning_goals: 30-degree endoscope camera navigation
Hand-eye coordination in endoscopic surgery
examples: 80 gynaecologists executed 30 trials of the 30-degree camera navigation exercise at three sites in Spain and Belgium
Exercises align with the GESEA Certification Programme's HYSTT model
key_sources: Hernansanz A, Rovira R, Basomba J, Comas R, Casals A. (2023). EndoTrainer: a novel hybrid training platform for endoscopic surgery. International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11548-023-02837-x

article_title: Effect of an endodontic e-learning application on students' performance during their first root canal treatment on real patients: a pilot study.
citation: Färber Christoph Maria, Lemos Martin, Said Yekta-Michael Sareh. (2022). Effect of an endodontic e-learning application on students’ performance during their first root canal treatment on real patients: a pilot study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-022-03463-y
title: Endodontic multimedia e-learning application with instructional videos on tooth models and patient cases
description: A multimedia learning application produced by the Audiovisual Media Centre of RWTH Aachen University, available via password-protected internet access to test group students. It contained "6 educational videos" demonstrating root canal treatments on DRSK RCT tooth models plus three patient-case videos, shortened to a maximum of 10 minutes with jump tags for section selection and tutor-recorded commentary. Students rated it 4.3 ± 0.6 on a 5-point Likert scale and 81.4 on the SUS.
requirements: Internet access and password authorization; videos produced according to departmental clinical standards and American Association of Endodontists guidelines
constraints: Available only to participating students of the test groups; study design did not distinguish the application's effect from the effect of the tooth models
target_learners: dental students in the initial clinical endodontic course
target_learning_goals: root canal treatment procedure knowledge and practical skills
examples: Test groups used the application alongside 48 h of practical hands-on training on extracted teeth, 7 h of theoretical seminars, and 16 h of lectures; 84 of 89 eligible students completed the evaluation (94% response rate)

article_title: Analysis of theoretical knowledge and the practice of science among Brazilian otorhinolaryngologists.
citation: de Mendonça Vitor Rosa Ramos, Alcântara Thiago, Andrade Nilvano, Andrade Bruno Bezerril, Barral-Netto Manoel, Boaventura Viviane. (2013). Analysis of theoretical knowledge and the practice of science among brazilian otorhinolaryngologists. Brazilian Journal of Otorhinolaryngology. https://doi.org/10.5935/1808-8694.20130087
title: Adapted questionnaire assessing scientific knowledge and practice among ENT specialists
description: A questionnaire adapted from the instrument of Reis-Filho et al. for undergraduate Medicine and Law students, keeping the scientific knowledge and practice questions and adding items on workplace, time since graduation, and physician-versus-resident status. It contains demographic items, six multiple-choice questions on "basic concepts of scientific method, statistics, and the structure of a scientific paper", and self-assessment items on interpreting, writing, planning and conducting research. It was answered anonymously at conference booths, with all questions required.
requirements: All questions had to be answered for inclusion; respondents answered only once and were not asked to identify themselves
constraints: Administered to volunteers recruited at two national otorhinolaryngology meetings in 2009 and 2010, a convenience sample of meeting attendees
target_learning_goals: assessment of theoretical scientific knowledge and self-assessed research competence
examples: Used in the 2013 cross-sectional study of 73 Brazilian ENT physicians and residents, yielding a mean 46.1% correct rate on the six theory questions

article_title: A Gastrointestinal Endoscopy Quality Control System Incorporated With Deep Learning Improved Endoscopist Performance in a Pretest and Post-Test Trial.
citation: Yao Liwen, Liu Jun, Wu Lianlian, Zhang Lihui, Hu Xiao, Liu Jinzhu, Lu Zihua, Gong Dexin, An Ping, Zhang Jun, Hu Guiying, Chen Di, Luo Renquan, Hu Shan, Yang Yanning, Yu Honggang. (2021). A Gastrointestinal Endoscopy Quality Control System Incorporated With Deep Learning Improved Endoscopist Performance in a Pretest and Post-Test Trial. Clinical and Translational Gastroenterology. https://doi.org/10.14309/ctg.0000000000000366
title: Endo.Adm: a fully automated deep-learning endoscopy audit-and-feedback system
description: Endo.Adm is a Python-based quality-control system coupled with three deep convolutional neural network models that automatically collects endoscopy images and pathology reports, computes quality indicators (withdrawal time, CIR, bowel preparation, PDR, ADR, photodocumented stomach sites, inspection time, GPC detection rate), and generates individual quality reports. It "consists of 3 main modules: data extraction, data staging, and data presenting." Data exchange uses DICOM standards, and endoscopists can log in on the department intranet to view their performance.
requirements: Access to an endoscopy information system and a pathology database through customized interface modules, with data exchange based on DICOM standards
constraints: Deep learning-based bowel preparation and withdrawal speed evaluation were not yet incorporated
Photodocumentation completeness statistics are based on still images rather than full-length videos
target_learning_goals: improving endoscopic quality indicators such as adenoma detection rate, withdrawal time, and photodocumentation completeness
examples: In the trial, feedback endoscopists received weekly customized quality report cards and could access the system for detailed quality statistics

article_title: A novel system for teaching the in-plane vascular access technique: A simulation study.
citation: Kikuchi M, Asao T, Tokumine J, Lefor AK, Matsushima H, Andoh H, Tanaka K, Kanamoto M, Ideno Y. (2021). A novel system for teaching the in-plane vascular access technique: a simulation study. Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000027201
title: Endoscope-equipped simulator with simultaneous endoscopic and ultrasound recording
description: The teaching system is a simulator device consisting of an ultrasound probe, a simulated vessel, a needle, and an endoscope connected to a computer to visualize the image inside the simulated vessel. An endoscope is inserted into the simulated vessel, and "Endoscopic and ultrasound views are recorded and saved in the computer simultaneously", enabling blinded expert evaluation of success, puncture accuracy, and needle tip visualization. Recordings were numbered and randomized by computer to conceal participant identity.
requirements: Recorded images must be measurable at different magnifications, with actual distances calculated using a magnification ratio derived from measured versus actual needle diameter
constraints: Images from 5 of 47 participants could not be used for accuracy evaluation (1 unclear, 4 computer error)
target_learners: health care providers learning ultrasound-guided vascular access
target_learning_goals: visualizing and evaluating needle position inside the vessel during in-plane puncture
examples: Used as the pre-test/post-test torso simulator (vessel diameter 6 mm, depth 10 mm) and the box-type training simulator (inner diameter 6 mm, depth 5 mm)
key_sources: Kikuchi M, Asao T, Tokumine J, Lefor AK, Matsushima H, Andoh H, Tanaka K, Kanamoto M, Ideno Y. (2021). A novel system for teaching the in-plane vascular access technique: a simulation study. Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000027201
